newsitem.title: GERMANY: LUFTHANSA TO HOLD SOME CARGO RATES.
newsitem.headline: LUFTHANSA TO HOLD SOME CARGO RATES.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG plans to hold some air cargo rates for shippers and give earlier warning of general rates rises, the Federation of German Industry (BDI) said.
The cargo airline had offered stable rates and longer contracts for industrial shippers during a meeting with the BDI air transport committee, a BDI statement said.
Lufthansa also agreed to tell air cargo shippers much earlier when it was planning to increase freight prices, the BDI added.
The airline has a number of long-term, direct contracts with large industrial firms although the bulk of its cargo space is sold by IATA agents, industry observers noted.
Committee chairman Dieter Oesau, formerly in charge of air cargo shipping for Siemens AG, told Lufthansa that fuel surcharges or any extra charges should in future be avoided.

His demand followed criticism by shippers last autumn and this spring of the airline's lack of notice before introducing and then removing a 10 cents per kg surcharge on air cargo rates due to soaring jet fuel prices.
Oesau also called on the air cargo industry to take shippers' needs more strongly into account or risk losing further market share to transport integrators.
"The offers of integrators are closely customer-orientated and were thus successful in the market. Such complete logistics concepts should enter the entire air cargo market," he said.
The BDI and Lufthansa Cargo agreed to hold regular meetings to discusss issues of common interest.
